
[1] the pending rendering is the real media, not a spinner card
  ok   a pending attachment asks for its picked bytes
  ok   the scanning card is now the FALLBACK (no local preview: another device, a reload, a non-media upload)
  ok   a pending media attachment carries the processing chip instead
  ok   and the chip cannot eat the lightbox tap or the player controls
  ok   a pending picture paints the picked bytes, falling back to its derived preview and then its own url
  ok   only a LOCAL copy or a pending upload counts as a stand-in — a clean file renders its own bytes and preview as before
  ok   the element still records the url it will fall back to
  ok   a clip is a player from the start, carrying the CLEAN source it will swap to
  ok   the download link and the star wait for the final bytes (nothing to save or star yet)
  ok   and that is what attDl does with the flag

[2] the verdict is applied to the element, never to the list
  ok   the per-attachment patch exists
  ok   and the per-message one that walks the slots
  ok   a slot list that no longer lines up is refused (the renderer rebuilds it)
  ok   each rendering is keyed by the attachment id, which survives a republish
  ok   an attachment whose KIND changed is refused
  ok   so is one whose reserved shape changed
  ok   the still swap compares the FILE the element is showing, not the url string
  ok   and the same file leaves the painted element exactly as it is (a republish in place must not re-decode it)
  ok   while the identity the menus and the lightbox read follows the published url
  ok   and holds the frame that is on screen until the new bytes land
  ok   a voice note moves its <audio> source, so the player keeps its position and chrome
  ok   the picked bytes are released once the published file is what is loaded — under the id AND the url the element was showing

[3] the wiring asks for the patch before it rebuilds
  ok   message-updated patches the attachments first
  ok   so does dm-updated (a DM photo or voice note must not blink either)
  ok   and the full rebuild is skipped for a message that is on screen
  ok   the "is this row painted" question is a helper of its own
  ok   the upload path registers the picked bytes against the attachment id, with its byte size for the cap
  ok   the preview store is bounded, and never evicts a file still sitting in a composer
  ok   the list reports which attachments it painted, so a preview dropped before posting is not kept forever
  ok   and a file still waiting on the slot keeps its picked bytes (never a spinner back where the picture is)

[4] pending: the picked bytes are on screen, with the chip
  ok   the picked bytes paint
  ok   the attachment renders inside its id-keyed slot
  ok   no spinner card — the media itself is what the reader sees
  ok   the picture paints the picked bytes while the slot holds the bytes back
  ok   and the processing chip says so
  ok   with nothing to download yet
  ok   the box is on screen at a real size (the stored 2500px shape, capped by CSS)

[5] the verdict swaps the bytes under the same node
  ok   the patch reports the change applied
  ok   the frame that was on screen is carried into the new box in the same tick
  ok   and it is the visible thing there
  ok   the box keeps its size across the swap

[6] a republish in place never re-points the painted picture
  ok   the patch reports the change applied
  ok   the painted source is untouched (no re-point, no re-decode, no blink)
  ok   while the identity the menus and the lightbox read moved to the published url
  ok   and so did the download link

[7] the frame on screen survives a slow preview
  ok   the picked bytes paint
  ok   the patch is applied even though the preview is in flight
  ok   the picture the reader was looking at is carried over, not replaced by an empty box
  ok   and the box keeps the reserved size while the request is open
  ok   the published preview really is in flight (the server is holding it)
  ok   while the chip is already gone (the verdict is known)
  ok   the swap lands when the bytes do
  ok   and the held frame goes with it
  ok   with the box still the same one

[8] a change the patch cannot make is refused, not half-applied
  ok   the pending row is rendered
  ok   a published shape that no longer matches the reserved one is refused (the list rebuilds instead)
  ok   and the row is left exactly as it was — never half-patched
  ok   a card that became a picture (a HEIC converted to JPEG) is refused too

[9] a voice note keeps its player
  ok   an audio url change patches in place
  ok   the <audio> is re-sourced to the published file
  ok   and the playhead was NOT reset (the player was not rebuilt)

[10] a clip settled in place keeps its player
  ok   the clip renders as a player
  ok   the patch reports the change applied
  ok   the SAME <video> element is still there (a replaced one restarts, and loses its poster)
  ok   and its source was never re-pointed at the same file
  ok   so its position survived too

[11] the verdict never takes a painted picture off the screen
  ok   the message on screen paints the picked bytes
  ok   the compressor verdict is applied to the element
  ok   the timeline has frames to judge
  ok   frame one: a painted picture in a sized box
  ok   no frame ever shows an unpainted box (or a scan card) where the picture is

  ok   and the row settles on the published bytes
  ok   with the processing chip gone

[12] the same, for the renderer fallback (when the patch refuses)
  ok   the picked bytes paint
  ok   the patch refuses the reshaped republish
  ok   the rebuilt row still paints the picked bytes with its chip (the renderer keeps the store too)
  ok   and the box it reserved is on screen, not a collapsed line

[13] the stylesheet carries the new pieces
  ok   .att-slot takes the row width, so the media inside resolves its reserved box against it (a shrink-to-fit slot collapses it)
  ok   the held frame is taken out of flow (no layout jump)
  ok   and a clip with no measured shape still shows its placeholder box (the wrap cannot collapse)
